statements.status_notes: zlib before 1.3.2 allows CPU consumption via crc32_combine64 and crc32_combine_gen64 because x2nmodp can do right shifts within a loop that has no termination condition.
statements.impact_statement: This zlib issue is tied to the crc32_combine64, crc32_combine_gen64, and x2nmodp code path. The Liquibase Secure image inherits the OS package from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (`docker/Dockerfile:2`) and the container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles, entrypoint scripts, and application source found no references to those zlib APIs, so the vulnerable code path is not reachable from the stock runtime.

statements.status_notes: zlib versions 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2 contain a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the gz_vacate() function when processing non-blocking gzwrite() operations with stale external buffer pointers. Attackers can trigger the overflow by calling gzprintf() or gzvprintf() after a write stall, causing an unchecked memmove() to write beyond the internal input buffer boundary.
statements.impact_statement: This heap buffer overflow requires an application to call system zlib's gzwrite/gzprintf APIs in a non-blocking configuration after a write stall. The JVM's own zip/gzip native code (libzip.so) bundles its own zip/deflate implementation and does not dynamically link against the system zlib package; a review of the JVM's native library dependencies confirmed no linkage against libz.
